reading.body:
Bill Hagerty's AI record in this data is one sponsored bill, a run of votes on a single unrelated bill, and $14,500 in PAC contributions from four large technology companies.

The contributions are the clearest pattern. Google's PAC gave $2,500 three times, in March 2025 and again in May 2026, and Amazon's PAC gave $2,500 twice, in March and April 2025. Meta and Intel each gave once, $2,500 and $2,000. Every dollar is dated before the August 2026 sponsorship of S. 5252, the BLADE Act on adversarial distillation. The data records the dates and the amounts and nothing about what was discussed or promised.

The votes are harder to read than the totals suggest. All eleven recorded votes concern S. 2296, and they fall on one day, October 9, 2025, plus three procedural votes in September. Hagerty voted both yea and nay on amendments to the same bill, which is ordinary for a amendment-by-amendment record and not evidence of a position on AI. The data does not say what S. 2296 does.

What this does not cover matters as much as what it does. There is no data here on data centers, power purchase agreements, grid interconnection, or permitting, which are the constraints that decide how fast AI compute gets built. A senator's AI record as captured here is legislative and financial, not infrastructural. The page also draws no link between any contribution and any vote, and the dates alone cannot establish one.
